answer: Admission needs a dispersion proof. For weeks the registry probes each candidate from independent vantage points, fitting replies into network coordinates; clones sharing one datacenter collapse into a dense knot and are cut. Each probe carries a fresh cipher, so recorded replies cannot be replayed, and the latency ripple must hold steady. A prism splits one beam into many colors, but no trick splits one hosting contract into many networks. Passing means renting live hosts across separate jurisdictions for months: a recurring bill, a paper trail, and a topology clustering still exposes.
